scope: read-only snapshot of the running Phase 12 Modal campaigns

counting_method.failed_attempt_definition: one stderr solveCurrentStep convergence-test failure line
counting_method.double_count_control: Each algorithm-specific solveCurrentStep line was counted once; the companion warning and StaticAnalysis lines from the same attempt were excluded.
counting_method.resume_limitation: The logs contain no evaluation identifier. Attempts re-executed after an interrupted, uncommitted epoch cannot be separated from first executions. They remain real operational solver work but cannot be deduplicated into unique logical evaluations.
counting_method.frequency_denominator: structural executions in the last durable per-seed epoch logs at the snapshot
counting_method.denominator_limitation: Warnings from the currently uncommitted epoch can precede the next durable structural-execution count, so frequency is an operational snapshot rather than an exact unique-evaluation incidence.

completed_seed_final_population_context.note: Final-population slots are not the full unique evaluation cache and cannot be correlated with warning-bearing evaluations.

recovery_measurement.reason: Neither stderr nor the persisted compact EvaluationResult records a common evaluation identifier with SolverAttempt data. The checkpoint stores only the final compact disposition and a hash of the transient Stage 2 result.

runtime_impact_measurement.reason: WorkerEvaluation elapsed_seconds is transient and is not persisted in checkpoints or seed results. Modal stderr has second-resolution warning timestamps but no evaluation start/end or evaluation identifier, so a causal duration comparison is not available.

controlled_evidence_check.use: The controlled published-design cases verify successful paths but provide no warning-bearing sample for estimating retry cost or recovery.

conclusion: Convergence fallback activity is frequent enough to be visible operationally: approximately 10.22 failed solver attempts were logged per 100 committed structural executions. The evidence does not support a recovery percentage or a runtime slowdown percentage. It therefore establishes nonzero retry work but cannot establish whether retries are a material share of total campaign runtime.
